He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois Fighting Illini]] and the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]]. ==High school career== Griffin attended [[Oak Park and River Forest High School]] in [[Oak Park, Illinois]] before moving to [[Ossining High School]] in [[Ossining (village), New York|Ossining, New York]], where he played basketball alongside [[Obi Toppin]].{{cite web |last1=Wagner |first1=Joey |title=Illinois basketball freshman Alan Griffin comes back home |url=https://herald-review.com/sports/illini/illinois-basketball-freshman-alan-griffin-comes-back-home/article_a7b92a11-eab2-5f7f-a55c-f6236651bd2b.html |website=[[Herald & Review]] |access-date=December 17, 2020 |date=October 31, 2018}}{{cite web |last1=Gutierrez |first1=Matthew |title=How Jimmy Butler and a life in basketball shaped Syracuse's Alan Griffin |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2201327/2020/11/17/syracuse-alan-griffin-basketball-jimmy-butler-role-model/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=December 17, 2020 |date=November 17, 2020}} For his final two years, he transferred to [[Archbishop Stepinac High School]] in [[White Plains, New York]]. As a senior, he averaged 19.2 points and 9.9 rebounds per game, shooting 48 percent from three-point range, and led his team to its first-ever New York State Federation Class AA title. Griffin also helped Stepinac win [[Catholic High School Athletic Association]] Archdiocesan and Class AA titles. He was named Player of the Year for [[Westchester County, New York|Westchester County]] and [[Putnam County, New York|Putnam County]] by ''[[The Journal News]]''.{{cite web |last1=Thomson |first1=Josh |title=Boys basketball: At Stepinac, Westchester/Putnam POY Alan Griffin delivered on his promise |url=https://www.lohud.com/story/sports/high-school/lohud-varsity-insider/2018/04/06/boys-basketball-stepinac-alan-griffin/456127002/ |website=[[The Journal News]] |access-date=December 17, 2020 |date=April 6, 2018}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] over offers from [[Fordham Rams men's basketball|Fordham]], [[Iona Gaels men's basketball|Iona]] and [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle]].{{cite web |last1=Ryan |first1=Shannon |title=Illinois receives commitment from Alan Griffin, son of former Bull Adrian Griffin |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-illinois-recruiting-alan-griffin-20180302-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=December 17, 2020 |date=March 2, 2018}} ==College career== As a freshman at Illinois, Griffin averaged 2.8 points in 8.1 minutes per game.{{cite web |last1=Ryan |first1=Shannon |title=Illini's Alan Griffin learned hard work from his NBA dad |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-illinois-basketball-alan-griffin-adrian-20200305-u4c2lbf5pfcobekiwhatvx2x6m-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=December 17, 2020 |date=March 5, 2020}} He became the team's [[sixth man]] as a sophomore. On February 27, he scored a season-high 24 points and six three-pointers in a 74–66 win over [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]].{{cite web |last1=Wagner |first1=Joey |title=Alan Griffin's career-high 24 points leads Illinois basketball to win over Northwestern |url=https://herald-review.com/sports/illini/alan-griffins-career-high-24-points-leads-illinois-basketball-to-win-over-northwestern/article_dee9b806-5168-5c29-85c2-b53e6076a985.html |website=[[Herald & Review]] |access-date=December 17, 2020 |date=February 28, 2020}} Griffin averaged 8.9 points and 4.5 rebounds per game per game.{{cite web |last1=Larson |first1=Mark |title=SU's Alan Griffin Meeting His Own Expectations |url=https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nys/central-ny/su-sports/2020/12/15/su-s-alan-griffin-meeting-his-own-expectations |website=[[Spectrum News]] |access-date=December 17, 2020 |date=December 15, 2020}} He led the [[NCAA Division I]] in [[offensive rating]] among players who were used in at least 20 percent of their team's possessions.{{cite web |last1=Emerman |first1=Danny |title=Proving It: Alan Griffin was the most efficient scorer in the nation. At SU, his role will grow. |url=http://dailyorange.com/2020/11/alan-griffin-was-most-efficient-scorer-his-role-will-grow-at-syracuse/ |website=[[The Daily Orange]] |access-date=December 17, 2020 |date=November 19, 2020}} After the season, Griffin transferred to [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] and received a waiver for immediate eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Waters |first1=Mike |title=Syracuse basketball's Alan Griffin receives transfer waiver from NCAA |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2020/08/syracuse-basketballs-alan-griffin-receives-transfer-waiver-from-ncaa.html |website=[[The Post-Standard]] |access-date=December 17, 2020 |date=August 18, 2020}} Through his first 5 games as a member of the Orange, he led the team in scoring with 18.4 points per game, and he led the team in points in 3 of those games, tallying 23, 20, and 22 points against [[Rider Broncs men's basketball|Rider]], [[2020–21 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]], and [[2020–21 Boston College Eagles men's basketball team|Boston College]] respectively. After going scoreless in the team's following game against [[Northeastern Huskies men's basketball|Northeastern]] on December 16, Griffin would have a huge comeback game on December 19 against [[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|Buffalo]], putting up 24 points, 10 rebounds, 3 assists, 2 steals and 3 blocks, including the game-saving rejection to send the game into [[Overtime (sports)|overtime]], which would eventually lead to an 11-point victory for Syracuse after being down by as many as 16 points.{{cite web |title=Orange Overcome 16-Pt. Deficit To Win In OT |url=https://cuse.com/news/2020/12/19/mens-basketball-orange-overcome-16-pt-deficit-to-win-in-overtime.aspx |website=cuse.com |access-date=December 20, 2020 |date=December 19, 2020}} Griffin averaged 13.3 points and 5.8 rebounds per game. Following the season he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite web |title=Syracuse's Alan Griffin to enter NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/news/syracuses-alan-griffin-to-enter-nba-draft |website=NBA.com |access-date=June 24, 2021 |date=April 30, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2021)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Griffin joined the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] after being acquired in a trade with the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] in October.{{cite news|first=Henry|last=Miller|title=New faces kick off Vipers training camp|url=https://myrgv.com/the-monitor/2021/10/26/new-faces-kick-off-vipers-training-camp/|work=[[The Monitor (Texas)|The Monitor]]|date=October 26, 2021|access-date=November 2, 2021}} However, he was waived on December 14 after 4 games.{{cite web|title=Vipers Make Roster Moves|url=https://riograndevalley.gleague.nba.com/news/vipers-make-roster-moves-2/|website=NBA.com|date=December 14, 2021|access-date=December 14, 2021}} ===Westchester Knicks (2021–2022)=== On December 19, 2021, Griffin signed with the [[Westchester Knicks]].{{cite news|first=Mike|last=Curtis|title=Former Syracuse guard Alan Griffin signs with G-League's Westchester Knicks|url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2021/12/former-syracuse-guard-alan-griffin-signs-with-g-leagues-westchester-knicks.html|work=[[The Post-Standard]]|date=December 20, 2021|access-date=December 20, 2021}} On January 9, 2022, Griffin was reacquired by the [[Westchester Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 9, 2022|access-date=January 9, 2022}} He was then later waived on January 23, 2022.{{cite Griffin's younger brother, [[AJ Griffin (basketball)|AJ]], Selected in the 16th pick in the 2022 draft. He has an older sister, Vanessa, and his younger sister, [[Aubrey Griffin|Aubrey]], plays college basketball for [[UConn Huskies women's basketball|UConn]].{{cite web |last1=Waters |first1=Mike |title=Meet the Griffins: How family helped shape Alan, Syracuse basketball's exciting newcomer |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2020/11/meet-the-griffins-how-family-helped-shape-alan-syracuse-basketballs-exciting-newcomer.html |website=[[The Post-Standard]] |access-date=December 16, 2020 |date=November 13, 2020}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://cuse.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/alan-griffin/19385 Syracuse Orange bio] *[https://fightingillini.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/alan-griffin/8088 Illinois Fighting Illini bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Griffin, Alan}} [[Category:2000 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:21st-century African-American sportsmen]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Canada]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Archbishop Stepinac High School alumni]] [[Category:Basketball players from Massachusetts]] [[Category:Basketball players from Westchester County, New York]] [[Category:Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball players]] [[Category:Newfoundland Growlers (basketball) players]] [[Category:People from Ossining, New York]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Waltham, Massachusetts]] [[Category:Rio Grande Valley Vipers players]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:Syracuse Orange men's basketball players]] [[Category:Westchester Knicks players]]
